messages:
Maya S: Quick async — posting a short status for kernel + continuous-batching + KV sprint. Need ownership clarifications and any blockers for tomorrow's canary. TL;DR: kernel PR merged but microbatch test flakes, KV warmup heuristic in review, continuous-batch perf at ~+8% in perf harness.
Omar H: Kernel PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123) merged this AM. Main outstanding is Jin's review on microbatch timing changes. I think we can cut a canary once jin okays or we revert the timing tweak.
Jin K: I repro the flaky test locally — `test_microbatch_alignment` fails when sequence padding varies. I put a debug patch in my fork and ran `pytest tests/test_microbatch.py::test_microbatch_alignment -k variable_pad -q` which showed timing drift. Will post a minimal repro later today. @Alex G can you double-check the cache eviction coupling? I suspect race with kv-evict.
Alex G: Looking. I saw one suspicious log: `kv_cache:evict: stale_ref_count=0 but pinned=true` in canary logs. I'm preparing a small fix that tightens the eviction precondition. PR coming (WIP) — link when ready. That should remove the race Jin is hitting.
Priya R: KV warmup heuristic PR is up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4138. It biases prefetch for hot prefixes using recent-30min histogram. Plan: land behind feature flag `kv.warmup.v2` and enable for canary only. A few notes: needs a migration to persist warmup counts and a perf check for cold-starts.
Maya S: Good. Can we list clear owners for the canary cut? Proposal:
- Kernel timing patch: Omar H (owner)
- Microbatch test fix / validation: Jin K (owner)
- KV eviction fix: Alex G (owner)
- KV warmup feature flag + migration: Priya R (owner)
- Canaries / rollout ops: Maya S + infra (coord)
If everyone ok, I'll kick the canary at 10:30 PT tomorrow.
Jin K: OK for owners. ETA for my repro + test fix: ~3pm today. If I can't get clean green, I'll open a revert-ready PR to hold the timing change out of canary.
Alex G: PR posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4142 — contains the eviction precondition and an extra unit test `test_evict_pinned`. PTAL. If it looks good to you @Jin K I'll merge and run full local microbatch suite.
Omar H: I can hold the kernel timing change behind a runtime flag as well (`kernel.microbatch.strict_timing`) so canary stays conservative. If Jin's fix lands we enable, otherwise flag=false.
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued by Maya S — target service `runtime-hotpath` image `sha:abcd1234`, initial weight 2% (staged windows 5m). Will post status updates.
Maya S: Ops checklist before I hit deploy:
- [ ] Alex merge eviction PR and confirm unit tests pass
- [ ] Jin green microbatch tests locally or revert-ready PR
- [ ] Priya enable `kv.warmup.v2` flag in canary config
- [ ] Confirm perf harness shows no >2% regression (current +8% improvement in perf harness but want to sanity-check infra noise)
I'll mark items as done in-thread as they happen.
Alex G: Done — merged eviction PR and ran `pytest tests/test_evict.py::test_evict_pinned -q` locally. All green. Marking checkbox.
Jin K: Quick update — repro reduced to a scheduling window; pushed a test fix to my branch and opened PR 4146. CI shows one flaky failure but it's unrelated networking teardown. Marking checkbox for my end (will monitor CI).
Priya R: Enabled `kv.warmup.v2=true` in the canary config I pushed to the ops repo. Also added a migration note in the PR description. Marking checkbox.
Maya S: All right — infra will watch canary metrics. If the microbatch or evict errors spike we'll rollback. deploy-bot please proceed at 10:30 PT unless abort flagged.
deploy-bot: canary started at 1742103000, weight=2%. Health checks passing (3/3) for first window. Will escalate on error.

Maya S: Thanks all — I'll follow up with a short postmortem if any regressions. Ping me @channel if anything critical before 10:30. :thumbsup:
